claims.text: UN News (5 June 2026), citing IOM: "nearly 1.5 million people without a stable place to live"; "more than 18,000 people" displaced in May 2026 alone from Cité Soleil attacks; the number of internally displaced people in Port-au-Prince rose "above 300,000" for the first time on record; "more than 110,000 Haitians" have been forcibly returned to the country since the beginning of 2026. IOM Chief of Mission Gregoire Goodstein: "Haiti's displacement crisis is entering an even more alarming phase."

Re-checked 12 August 2026: OCHA's 'Haiti: Nationwide Humanitarian Response (1-30 June 2026)' report (ReliefWeb, published 29 July 2026) confirms the 1.47 million/IOM Round 13 DTM figure (a 1 percent increase over Round 12) as the still-current national displacement total, including more than 300,000 in the Port-au-Prince metropolitan area alone, and adds that a new wave of violence between 13-19 June forced over 5,000 additional people to flee Cite Soleil -- a component of, not a supersession of, the national total. UN News (6 August 2026) restates the BINUH figures already on file (613 killed, 375 injured, 176+ women and girls raped over 4.5 months through 31 July) without a newer nationwide aggregate.

UN News (6 August 2026): in Plaine du Cul-de-Sac and Cite Soleil alone, at least 613 people were killed and 375 injured over a 4.5-month period through 31 July 2026, more than a third of them not associated with gangs (including 111 women and 77 children); over 18,000 people were displaced from those two neighbourhoods in the same period, and 176+ women and girls were reported raped by gang members, often as a form of punishment. The 13 June attack on a World Cup viewing crowd of about 300 people killed 61 and injured 20, including at least 7 children.

UN Security Council briefing (S/2026/574, 20 July 2026, per press.un.org): only 1,000 of the 5,550 authorized troops for the Gang Suppression Force have been deployed; the UN verified 2,088 grave violations against children in 2025. SRSG Carlos Ruiz Massieu reaffirmed that about 1.5 million people have been forced to flee their homes because of gang violence.

UN News (25 August 2026), citing a new BINUH quarterly report covering April-June 2026: at least 1,408 people were killed and 656 injured nationwide, with more than half the casualties attributed to gangs and about 40 percent occurring during security operations; 463 people were killed in fighting in the Plaine du Cul-de-Sac and Cité Soleil area; at least 796 people were documented as victims of gang-related rape; and at least 81 people were abducted for ransom during the quarter. By May, nearly 1.47 million people were internally displaced across Haiti, more than half of them children. The article states the Gang Suppression Force 'has yet to be fully deployed.'

UN News (25 August 2026): a gang attack that began late Sunday, 23 August 2026, on the farming community of Kenscoff, south of Port-au-Prince, killed at least 47 people and wounded 22 -- one of the deadliest recent attacks on what had been a relatively peaceful area.

UN press release SG/SM/23248 (25 August 2026), statement by the Spokesman for Secretary-General António Guterres: "The Secretary-General condemns the latest gang attack on Kenscoff, a commune on the outskirts of Port-au-Prince, in Haiti, that reportedly killed at least 47 people during the night of 23 August, including 22 who were reportedly executed in a church compound where they had found shelter." The Secretary-General called for Haitian authorities to ensure accountability, "including through the specialized judicial units, recently created with international support to investigate mass crimes."

UN Security Council transcript of its 10216th meeting on Haiti (28 August 2026): Acting Assistant Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs Indrika Ratwatte told the Council that in the Kenscoff attack of 23-24 August, "dozens of people were killed and more than 2,600 forced to flee their homes ... over 50 people were reportedly abducted"; nationwide, "nearly 1.5 million people, 12% of Haiti's population, are internally displaced," more than 5,500 incidents of gender-based violence have been recorded in the first six months of 2026 (about 70% involving rape), the recruitment and use of children by armed groups rose an estimated 200% in 2025, and more than 1,600 schools remain closed, affecting 7,500 teachers and depriving more than 240,000 students. Special Representative and BINUH head Carlos Ruiz Massieu reported "more than 1,400 people killed and more than 600 injured between April and June 2026," and Argentina's representative cited "more than 3,000 deaths so far in 2026."

UN Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs (28 August 2026): Special Representative of the Secretary-General Carlos Ruiz Massieu welcomed "increased coordination among the Haitian National Police, Haitian Armed Forces and Gang Suppression Force" following the Kenscoff massacre and called for its "swift and full deployment," stressing that security operations must be accompanied by restoration of State authority, rebuilt basic services, schools and health facilities, economic livelihood programmes, pathways for youth to leave gangs, and accountability for those perpetrating and financing gang violence.

UN News (19 July 2026): "1.47 million people have fled their homes largely due to violence." During a Cité Soleil violence outbreak, "at least 542 people were killed and 355 injured," and "at least 176 women and girls were raped." Separately, at least 87 deaths have been reported from vigilante killings of suspected gang collaborators. "Around 6.4 million people need humanitarian assistance" and "more than 5.8 million people are expected to go hungry this year."

UN News (20 July 2026), 'LIVE: Haiti endures violence and hunger, but hopes grow for a more secure future': reconfirms IOM's nearly-1.5-million displacement figure (originally reported 5 June 2026) as still current, reports on a UN Security Council discussion of the Gang Suppression Force, and notes that Haitian security forces have begun recording limited successes against armed gangs, pushing some criminal groups out of strategic locations in Port-au-Prince and reopening some major roads; the article provides no updated death-toll or displacement aggregate beyond the figures already reported. Re-checked 5 August 2026: no newer UN News, ReliefWeb, or OCHA report supersedes the 19-20 July 2026 figures (1.47M displaced, 542 killed in the Cité Soleil outbreak, 6.4M in humanitarian need, 5.8M facing hunger).

New localized report found 8 August 2026: a BINUH (UN Integrated Office in Haiti) report posted to ReliefWeb 6 August 2026 states that, in the Plaine du Cul-de-Sac area and Cite Soleil specifically, "between 6 March and 31 July 2026, at least 613 people were killed and 375 others injured, primarily during confrontations between criminal gangs... more than 176 women and girls were subjected to rape, including gang rape" and "more than 18,000 people [were] forced to flee their homes" in that area; it also documents an attack after a 13 June FIFA World Cup match that killed at least 61 people. This is a more specific, localized casualty count for a sub-national area and period, and does not supersede the nationwide IOM displacement total (1.47 million) or the broader 19 July UN News Cite Soleil figure (542 killed) already cited, which cover different scopes; no newer nationwide displacement aggregate has been published.

OCHA's Latin America & the Caribbean Weekly Situation Update (7 August 2026) reports that armed violence in Saint-Michel de l'Attalaye, Artibonite department, displaced approximately 4,216 people on 28 July, with three displacement sites forced to close, triggering additional secondary displacement — a new localized incident that does not supersede the nationwide IOM displacement total (1.47 million) already on file.

A UN Integrated Office in Haiti (BINUH) and OHCHR report published 6 August 2026 on ReliefWeb documents that, between 6 March and 31 July 2026, 'at least 613 people were killed and 375 others injured, primarily during confrontations between criminal gangs' specifically in the Plaine du Cul-de-Sac area and Cite Soleil -- a regional sub-total, not a national figure, so it is not used to overwrite this record's national death toll. More than a third of the regional victims were not gang-affiliated, including 111 women and 77 children, and more than 176 women and girls were subjected to rape, including gang rape, by gang members. The national displacement figure of nearly 1.5 million remains the latest confirmed IOM/DTM total found on ReliefWeb (originally reported 5 June 2026); no newer national total was located as of 10 August 2026.

description: Gang violence in Haiti has killed more than 3,000 people nationwide so far in 2026 and displaced nearly 1.5 million, with an attack on Kenscoff, south of Port-au-Prince, killing 47 and displacing thousands more on 23-24 August. Briefing the UN Security Council on 28 August, BINUH head Carlos Ruiz Massieu reported at least 1,408 killed and 656 injured nationwide from April through June, while OCHA's Indrika Ratwatte said nearly 1.5 million people (12% of the population) are displaced, over 5,500 gender-based violence incidents have been recorded this year (about 70% rape), and more than 1,600 schools remain closed, depriving over 240,000 students. The Kenscoff attack killed at least 47 -- including 22 reportedly executed inside a church compound -- displaced more than 2,600 and left over 50 abducted, one of the largest mass kidnappings in Haiti in recent years; Guterres condemned the attack, and Ruiz Massieu has called for the Gang Suppression Force's swift, full deployment alongside restored State authority and accountability. About 6.4 million people need humanitarian assistance and more than 5.8 million face hunger this year.

impact.summary: Briefing the UN Security Council on 28 August 2026, Argentina's representative cited more than 3,000 deaths nationwide in Haiti so far in 2026, while BINUH head Carlos Ruiz Massieu put the April-June quarterly toll at more than 1,400 killed and more than 600 injured. OCHA's Indrika Ratwatte told the Council that nearly 1.5 million people (12% of the population) remain internally displaced, more than 5,500 incidents of gender-based violence have been recorded this year (about 70% involving rape), child recruitment by armed groups rose an estimated 200% in 2025, and more than 1,600 schools remain closed, depriving over 240,000 students. The 23-24 August gang attack on Kenscoff killed at least 47 people, displaced more than 2,600 and saw over 50 people abducted; the Gang Suppression Force remains under-deployed despite calls from the Secretary-General's Special Representative for its swift, full deployment.

location.region: Nationwide, concentrated in Port-au-Prince metropolitan area (incl. Cité Soleil, Drouillard)

name: Gang Violence Displacement Crisis — Haiti

UN Secretary-General António Guterres condemned the Kenscoff attack in a 25 August 2026 statement, confirming that of the 47 people killed, 22 were reportedly executed inside a church compound where they had sought shelter, and called for accountability through Haiti's specialized judicial units for mass crimes.

A BINUH quarterly report (Apr-Jun 2026, per UN News 25 Aug 2026) found at least 1,408 people killed and 656 injured nationwide, with 463 killed and 796 gang-rape victims in Plaine du Cul-de-Sac/Cite Soleil; separately, a gang attack on Kenscoff, south of Port-au-Prince, that began late on 23 August killed at least 47 people and wounded 22.

A BINUH/OHCHR report published 6 August 2026 documented at least 613 people killed and 375 injured in Plaine du Cul-de-Sac and Cite Soleil between 6 March and 31 July 2026, more than a third of them not gang-affiliated, plus 176+ women and girls raped and over 18,000 people displaced from those areas; a 13 June attack on a World Cup viewing crowd killed 61.

OCHA's nationwide humanitarian response report for June 2026 (published 29 July) held the national displacement total at IOM's Round 13 figure of 1.47 million — more than 300,000 of them in the Port-au-Prince metropolitan area — and recorded that a new wave of violence between 13-19 June forced over 5,000 additional people to flee Cite Soleil.

Armed violence in Saint-Michel de l'Attalaye, Artibonite department, displaced approximately 4,216 people on 28 July and forced three displacement sites to close, triggering secondary displacement, per OCHA's weekly situation update of 7 August 2026.

A UN Security Council briefing of 20 July 2026 reported that only 1,000 of the 5,550 authorized troops for the Gang Suppression Force had deployed; SRSG Carlos Ruiz Massieu reaffirmed that about 1.5 million people have been forced from their homes by gang violence.
